stories.title: UK government’s obesity plan ‘doomed to fail’, MPs warn
stories.summary: Cross-party committee says ‘moonshot’ vow to end obesity epidemic in a decade will fail without personal leadership from PM The UK government’s promise to reverse rising obesity rates in the next decade is “doomed to fail” without a major rethink and a new plan led directly by the prime minister, a cross-party committee of MPs has concluded. The health and social care select committee said in a report that there are no signs the so-called “moonshot ambition on obesity”, set out in the 10-year health plan for England, will achieve anything significant. stories.title: Battle lines redrawn in Spain’s snap election after latest train disaster
stories.summary: Next month’s poll no longer the contest it was, as Pedro Sánchez finds himself forced to defend government’s safety record One of the most dependable cliches of contemporary Spanish politics is that it never pays to bet against Pedro Sánchez . Time and time again – as leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers’ party (PSOE) and as prime minister – Sánchez has shown an almost preternatural ability to profit from adversity, and to confound expectations and wrongfoot his opponents. But next month’s snap general election , called by Sánchez after rightwing and far-right parties voted down the housing reforms his coalition government had announced in response to angry protests , may suddenly not be the contest it once was. stories.title: TUC leader expects wave of union recognition in private sector over coming year

From Friday, as part of Labour’s Employment Rights Act, unions will have the right to enter workplaces or communicate with staff electronically. From January, employers will be obliged to inform workers of their right to join a union. Continue reading...

stories.title: Security guard who protected Nigel Farage on campaign trail was facing rape charge
